name: Dynamic Programming Table
summary: Fill a table dp[i][j] = 'is s[i..j] a palindrome?'. Every single character is a palindrome (the diagonal); a longer span is a palindrome when its two ends match and the span just inside it already is. Track the longest true span.
visualizationIntent: init: an n x n table; the diagonal (single characters) lights green. loop: fill spans of increasing length; the current (i,j) cell reads its inner (i+1,j-1) neighbour. check: if the ends match and the inner span is a palindrome, mark (i,j) true. update: track the longest true span and keep its cell gold. return: the substring for the best span.

lineExplanations.5: Add one table row per character...
lineExplanations.11: A single character is always a palindrome.
lineExplanations.12: Move to the next diagonal cell.
lineExplanations.14: Grow the span length up to n.
lineExplanations.15: Slide the span start back to 0.
lineExplanations.16: Try every span of this length.
lineExplanations.19: Length-2 spans need no inner check.
lineExplanations.20: Otherwise the inner span must already be a palindrome.
lineExplanations.21: The inner span is a palindrome, so this one can be too.
lineExplanations.22: A span is a palindrome when ends match and the inside is one.
lineExplanations.23: Mark this span as a palindrome.
lineExplanations.24: Is this the longest palindrome so far?
lineExplanations.28: Move on to the next length.

syntaxExplanations.1: class Solution: defines the class wrapper expected by the platform.
syntaxExplanations.2: def longestPalindrome(self, s): receives the string s.
syntaxExplanations.3: n = len(s) stores the string length.
syntaxExplanations.4: dp = [] will become the n x n palindrome table.
syntaxExplanations.5: for i in range(n): builds one row per character.
syntaxExplanations.6: dp.append([0] * n) adds a row of falses.
syntaxExplanations.7: best_lo = 0 marks the best palindrome's start.
syntaxExplanations.8: best_len = 1 starts the best length at 1 (single char).
syntaxExplanations.10: while i < n: seeds every single character.
syntaxExplanations.11: dp[i][i] = 1 marks each single character a palindrome.
syntaxExplanations.12: i = i + 1 advances along the diagonal.
syntaxExplanations.14: while length <= n: grows the span length.
syntaxExplanations.15: i = 0 restarts the span start for this length.
syntaxExplanations.16: while i + length - 1 < n: iterates spans that fit.
syntaxExplanations.17: j = i + length - 1 is the span's right end.
syntaxExplanations.18: ends_match = s[i] == s[j] compares the two ends.
syntaxExplanations.19: inner_ok = length == 2 is true for two-char spans.
syntaxExplanations.20: if dp[i + 1][j - 1] == 1: checks the inner span.
syntaxExplanations.21: inner_ok = True when the inner span is a palindrome.
syntaxExplanations.22: if ends_match and inner_ok: is the palindrome condition.
syntaxExplanations.23: dp[i][j] = 1 marks the span a palindrome.
syntaxExplanations.24: if length > best_len: is true for a new longest.
syntaxExplanations.25: best_len = length records the new longest length.
syntaxExplanations.26: best_lo = i records where it starts.
syntaxExplanations.27: i = i + 1 slides the span start right.
syntaxExplanations.28: length = length + 1 moves to the next span length.
syntaxExplanations.29: result = s[best_lo:best_lo + best_len] extracts the answer.
syntaxExplanations.30: return result hands back the longest palindromic substring.
